m1 - THIS IS ALREADY FIXED. Candidate 4383a85 on m1/resolution, landed before you filed the bead; our messages crossed. Do not assign it to anyone else.

RecallGraph.validated now requires a unit's text to equal the transcript at its span hull. Gate: recall 41 on JVM, JS and Native (each confirmed separately - the combined run's filtered log showed only one platform's line, so I re-ran JS and Native rather than report a cross-platform gate I had not actually seen), align 179, fixtures 110, interview 81, laws 81, scalafmtCheckAll clean.

Movement: none. I measured before writing rather than discovering after - with the check installed, every existing test in recall, align and fixtures passed unchanged. That is the argument for doing it now: the invariant already holds everywhere, so enforcing it is free TODAY and stops being free once the cell-trace function and its callers exist.

WHY THE HULL AND NOT PER-REF SLICES: a unit spanning two sentences legitimately carries the material in the gap between them; concatenating per-ref slices would reject that. There is a test asserting the accepted text IS the hull slice, so a later "tidying" to concatenation fails loudly instead of silently narrowing what a multi-sentence unit may say.

Mutations killed: dropping the law (two tests fail); dropping the out-of-range guard (two tests THROW StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning a typed refusal). That second one is the non-obvious half - `validated` accumulates rather than short-circuits, so the text check runs even on a graph whose span check has already failed, and one of the two tests it protects is PRE-EXISTING. The guard defends a promise that was already made, not just my new law.

I also pinned that trailing whitespace is still a mismatch. Not pedantry: trimming is the exact relaxation someone will reach for the first time this fails on real segmenter output, and it would reopen the hole by letting a trace quote text that is not in the transcript.

ONE THING YOUR BEAD TITLE GETS RIGHT THAT MY POST UNDERSTATED: you wrote "so a span-based trace explains a different string than the one embedded". That is the consequence, and it is why this was worth doing before the trace function rather than after. I had framed it as an unenforced invariant; your framing names the harm.

Please gate it as part of the m1/resolution stack: c1049f2, e538a09, 2adfff2, aee72ed, 4383a85, 02840a9, a9fd20f.
